title: Tag Link Management Delivery
summary: narrow New Tag preflight, migrate tags to canonical public document URLs, and deliver shared published-document search plus Tag Registry link management
content_html:
Tag Link Management Delivery

Target Result

Tag Registry stores an ordered array of optional one-way canonical document locations for each tag. Tag Registry and Edit Tag present current document titles, Edit Tag can search published document titles and add a selected location through a reusable picker or remove an association, and the registry no longer stores or presents a tag description. Tag Editor searches published Analysis locations only. Report context appears in those picker results when present; scope context appears only for consumers configured with more than one scope.

The relationship and independent-lifecycle boundary remains owned by Tag-document linking.

Before that UI is implemented, New Tag stops auditing every existing registry association. Its job remains one atomic result: validate the submitted tag, allocate and create one fresh Analysis tags document, append the new linked registry row, rebuild the child projection, and report the outcome. The later schema cutover records that freshly created canonical location at doc_url[0].

Status And Order

Current state: planned. TLM-1's pre-implementation contract is accepted; TLM-0 remains the only ready implementation checkpoint. Complete TLM-0, record focused evidence, and stop for review before starting schema or UI work. No further interaction design is required before implementation and realistic use.

Review rule: TLM-1 records an already accepted planning decision, not shipped behavior. Complete implementation checkpoints TLM-0 and TLM-2 through TLM-5 in order, record evidence beneath each checkpoint, and stop for review before starting the next.

Frozen Data Contract

The next registry schema uses doc_url as an ordered array of canonical same-origin Docs Viewer locations:

{
  "doc_url": [
    "/analysis/?doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=d-20260727-225608-63967a",
    "/docs/?scope=studio&doc=d-20260729-151446-09489e"
  ]
}
  • doc_url: [] means the tag is not linked. New Tag writes its newly created Analysis tags location at index 0; later picker selections append in commit order.
  • The URL is the association identity because it preserves the chosen report context. The same source document may therefore appear more than once through different canonical report URLs.
  • The same canonical URL cannot occur twice within one tag, but any number of tags may reference it. Add and remove operations identify the complete URL rather than relying on a mutable array index.
  • A canonical URL is a normalized repository-relative viewer route produced by Docs ownership. It includes the configured viewer base and scope behavior, the exact report-host document where applicable, and the exact displayed document. It excludes fragments, transient filters, and arbitrary query state unless a later contract deliberately makes them part of location identity.
  • It never stores a scheme or host. The same root-relative value resolves against the local origin while working locally and the public origin after publication.
  • Each scope uses its configured canonical viewer base. Analysis locations use /analysis/?doc=<report-doc-id>&subdoc=<document-id>; they do not store a local /docs/?scope=analysis... alternative. A scope whose canonical base is /docs/ still uses that configured route.
  • New writes accept only a URL returned by the supported document-location provider. They do not accept free-form, external, or merely parseable URLs.
  • Stale URLs remain stored, visible, and removable. No title match, selected parent, displayed document, or alternative report may silently replace them.

The registry does not store document or report titles. A shared document-location provider resolves each stored URL to current presentation data such as {url, scope_id, document_title, report_title, available}. Picker results represent actual report placements, not just documents: the same source document may appear as separate choices such as bird-nerve — All Tags and bird-nerve — Made-up Tags.

The provider searches public projections, not management or source collections. Its initial coverage is published Analysis and Library documents plus their configured published sub-scopes. The picker adapter requires a non-empty consumer-supplied scopeIds allowlist and has no implicit all-supported-scopes default. Tag Editor supplies ["analysis"]. The provider loads and returns only records from the requested supported scopes. Top-level public search records and sub-scope placement records contribute one searchable result per canonical URL. Hidden, manage-only, local-only, and unpublished documents are absent, so every new selection has a public route that also resolves against the local origin during local work.

Provider records always retain scope_id. A picker configured with one scope omits the redundant scope label; a picker configured with more than one shows it. Report context remains visible when present because distinct report placements can have distinct canonical URLs. Scope-label visibility follows the configured allowlist length, not the scopes represented by the current query results.

The picker commits one reusable result such as {url, scope_id, document_title, report_title}. Consumer adapters determine how it is written:

  • Tag Registry stores url in doc_url[] and Tag Editor renders it as the title link.
  • Ordinary document authoring inserts url as the destination of a Markdown link.
  • A future document-capable Semantic Token adapter uses url as the generated target-lookup href; Semantic Token source continues to store its registered token identity rather than embedding a raw URL in token syntax.

These are three uses of the same selected canonical URL, not three picker or route contracts. Plain-link and Semantic Token authoring remain later consumers; this delivery proves the shared result through Tag Registry first.

Frozen Interaction Contract

  • Edit Tag shows doc_url[] as a selectable title-only list in array order. Rows retain their exact URL internally; identical visible titles need no extra disambiguation after selection.
  • Add document opens the picker with scopeIds: ["analysis"]. The picker searches published Analysis titles, omits the redundant Analysis scope label, and shows report context when present so the user can choose the intended canonical location. Committing a result appends its URL and returns to Edit Tag. A later consumer configured with several scopes shows scope context too.
  • The picker excludes an exact URL already present in the draft. A different URL with the same document title remains a valid result.
  • Selecting a linked-document row enables Remove link. Removal changes only the modal draft; it does not delete the document or mutate canonical data.
  • Edit Tag Confirm writes the complete revised doc_url[] with the other accepted tag edits in one atomic registry mutation. Cancel discards all draft additions and removals.
  • A URL that no longer resolves is shown as Unavailable document, remains selectable, and can be removed. The stored URL is not repaired or replaced.
  • The Tag Registry table replaces description with documents. It renders document titles as comma-separated links in doc_url[] order and renders — for an empty array. Equal titles remain equal; no report label is added.
  • Remove link is deliberately distinct from Tag or document deletion.

This is the final pre-implementation interaction decision. Ordinary-width and narrow-width fit, tactile selection behavior, and final wording are reviewed against the working UI rather than designed further in the abstract.

The schema cutover retires the tag-row description field. This does not alter alias descriptions or the independent contents of existing linked documents.

TLM-0 Prerequisite Contract

The current creation planner calls registry_document_ids, which validates the complete registry as though New Tag owns association integrity. It rejects creation when any existing row has a missing, duplicate, non-immutable, or non-resolving doc_id.

That is wider than the creation responsibility:

submitted New Tag
  -> validate new tag_id, scalar group, and description
  -> reject an existing tag_id
  -> allocate one fresh document identity
  -> create one new document and linked row atomically
  -> rebuild the exact Analysis/tags projection

existing registry associations
  -> preserve unchanged
  -> do not audit or repair during New Tag

TLM-0 is deliberately limited to that current-schema prerequisite. description removal and doc_url[] creation start after its review gate.

New Tag retains the guards required for its own write:

  • require the supported registry version and a registry tags array;
  • validate the submitted fields and reject an existing tag_id;
  • resolve the configured direct-child document root and confine the new path;
  • allocate the immutable ID directly from the document timestamp and cryptographic token, without supplying registry or source identities; and
  • preserve the existing atomic Registry/document write, targeted rebuild, compensation, activity, response, and manual-patch contracts.

The planner does not inspect any existing registry doc_id, inventory document IDs for allocation, compare the generated ID with registry rows, or preflight the destination's existence. write_text_atomic_new is the sole collision boundary: it refuses to overwrite a real destination if the generated identity does collide. That create-only write is filesystem safety, not registry association validation. Focused association audit and repair belong to the later link-management workflow.

Delivery Tracker

[ ] TLM-0 — Narrow New Tag To Its Own Write

  • [ ] Remove registry_document_ids and all other existing-association reads from document-ID allocation and row creation.
  • [ ] Stop inventorying Analysis document IDs or checking destination existence before the exclusive-create write.
  • [ ] Keep validation of the new tag, new row, new immutable document ID, configured source root, confined path, and atomic create-only destination.
  • [ ] Prove creation succeeds while unrelated existing rows include:
    • no doc_id;
    • a shared doc_id;
    • a stale doc_id; and
    • a malformed doc_id.
  • [ ] Preserve duplicate-new-tag_id, invalid submitted field, destination collision at exclusive create, write/rebuild failure, compensation, response, activity, and manual-patch behavior.
  • [ ] Remove helpers and tests whose only purpose was whole-registry or whole-collection document-ID preflight.
  • [ ] Run focused creation/planner/API tests and the narrow maintained Tag Registry smoke boundary.
  • [ ] Record exact tested and untested surfaces and inspect the final diff.

Checkpoint / review gate: New Tag creates one correct linked tag/document pair without certifying unrelated associations. No links UI, association mutation, repair, or presentation change starts before user review.

[x] TLM-1 — Freeze The Cutover And Interaction

  • [x] Use one-way tag_registry_v4 to tag_registry_v5 migration with no dual-schema compatibility path.
  • [x] Support published Analysis and Library documents plus their configured published sub-scopes behind a required consumer scope allowlist; Tag Editor requests Analysis only. Exclude Studio, manage-only, local-only, hidden, and unpublished documents.
  • [x] Use one shared title-search picker whose records retain scope/report context and commit one canonical URL plus presentation data. Omit scope from one-scope presentation while retaining report context.
  • [x] Keep the Edit Tag linked-document list title-only and permit equal titles.
  • [x] Use draft Add document and Remove link actions, then commit the complete URL array only on Edit Tag confirmation.
  • [x] Replace the registry description column with comma-separated document title links and an empty-state dash.
  • [x] Keep stale URLs visible as Unavailable document and removable without repair.

Checkpoint accepted: the persistence, search, modal, table, and downstream consumer contracts are frozen. Visual and tactile acceptance waits for the working UI.

[ ] TLM-2 — Cut Over The Registry And New Tag

Start only after TLM-0 is accepted.

  • [ ] Add tag_registry_v5 validation for ordered canonical doc_url arrays.
  • [ ] Migrate each nonblank v4 scalar to its current canonical Analysis tags report URL; migrate a missing or blank scalar to [].
  • [ ] Remove tag-row description during the same guarded migration while preserving row order, tag_id, scalar group, timestamps, policy, aliases, assignments, documents, and document content.
  • [ ] Reject noncanonical, unsupported, external, and within-tag duplicate new URLs without rejecting shared URLs across different tags.
  • [ ] Remove description from New Tag input, validation, registry writes, direct API and manual-patch contracts. A new document starts from its tag title without a duplicated registry description.
  • [ ] Record the freshly created Analysis tags canonical URL at doc_url[0] without reading existing URL arrays for uniqueness or stale-link checks.
  • [ ] Preserve TLM-0's exclusive-create collision boundary, atomic registry and document write, rebuild, compensation, activity, and failure behavior.
  • [ ] Remove v4-only readers and writers after the migration; do not retain a compatibility alias or silent scalar/URL normalization in the live app.
  • [ ] Reconcile the canonical migration and run focused schema, migration, creation, API, rollback, and manual-patch evidence.

Checkpoint / review gate: canonical v5 data and New Tag are accepted before association mutation or browser picker integration.

[ ] TLM-3 — Deliver The Shared Document Location Provider And Picker

  • [ ] Add the reusable local-authoring document-location picker under shared/frontend/, using the existing shared search-list behavior rather than creating another listbox implementation.
  • [ ] Keep the picker independent of a route shell so Tag Registry and later local authoring consumers can provide their own adapters.
  • [ ] Require each consumer to supply a non-empty scopeIds allowlist. Keep supported-collection policy, durable form state, and writes with the consuming app; keep the low-level shared search-list record-only. The picker passes the allowlist to the provider and commits one exact canonical URL plus presentation data; it does not serialize Tag Registry values, Markdown links, or Semantic Tokens itself.
  • [ ] Add a compact public document-location search projection and provider for published Analysis and Library documents plus their published sub-scopes. Load and return only requested supported scopes, fail closed for empty or unsupported scope requests, and emit one canonical root-relative URL per actual placement with its document, scope, and report presentation data.
  • [ ] Build from public search/index and sub-scope placement ownership only. Do not read manage manifests, local published workspaces, source front matter, or local Docs APIs in the picker.
  • [ ] Permit one source document to appear in several provider records when distinct report-host documents surface it. Do not construct a report/document cross-product or assume one report host per sub-scope.
  • [ ] Search document titles case-insensitively as the user types, rank exact and prefix matches ahead of other title matches, and preserve distinct placements with duplicate titles.
  • [ ] Support asynchronous loading, keyboard/pointer commit, empty results, and provider failure. Retain scope on every record; show it only when scopeIds.length > 1. Show report context when present. Do not vary scope-label visibility from the current result set.
  • [ ] Exclude exact URLs already attached to the edited tag from selectable results while preserving them in the existing-link list.
  • [ ] Add pure component/provider, public-projection, and exact route/module wiring evidence.

Checkpoint / review gate: approve provider results and picker behavior before allowing the picker to mutate Tag Registry.

[ ] TLM-4 — Integrate Tag Link Management

  • [ ] Add focused atomic append/remove operations using explicit tag_id plus the complete draft doc_url[]; confirmation changes only the associations and accepted tag fields and never deletes a document.
  • [ ] Preserve unrelated tag rows, URL order, aliases, assignments, documents, and document content.
  • [ ] Replace the Tag Registry description heading, cells, and sort projection with documents, rendering current titles as comma-separated links in URL order and — for no links.
  • [ ] Remove tag-description controls and state from New Tag and Edit Tag.
  • [ ] Render zero, one, or many title-only selectable linked-document rows in Edit Tag. Equal titles remain unchanged and rows retain exact URL identity.
  • [ ] Add Add document to open the shared picker with scopeIds: ["analysis"] and append one committed URL to the draft. Omit the redundant scope label and retain report context in picker results.
  • [ ] Add Remove link, disabled without a selection, to remove the selected exact URL from the draft without deleting a document.
  • [ ] Commit the complete URL draft atomically on Edit Tag confirmation and discard it on cancel.
  • [ ] Render an unresolved URL as Unavailable document in both surfaces while keeping it selectable, linked to its exact stored URL, and removable.
  • [ ] Never accept free-form IDs or URLs and never infer a location from the displayed document, selected tree row, title, group, or an alternative route.
  • [ ] Add focused planner, API, atomic-write, activity, failure, retry, frontend-domain, and route-module evidence before realistic UI review.
  • [ ] Review realistic linked, unlinked, multi-link, shared, duplicate-title, multi-report, search-no-match, provider-failure, and stale examples at ordinary and narrow widths.

Checkpoint / review gate: user acceptance of the actual title list, picker, remove interaction, and state language before closeout.

[ ] TLM-5 — Integration And Closeout

  • [ ] Run the accumulated focused service, API, route-module, and maintained Tag Registry checks chosen by the accepted interaction.
  • [ ] Verify migration, optional, ordered, shared, stale, duplicate-title, multi-report, and standalone-document behavior without implying synchronization or exclusive ownership.
  • [ ] Inspect the final source and generated diff independently.
  • [ ] Move only stable shipped behavior and remaining weak spots into Tag Registry and Tag Source Data.
  • [ ] Close or split any unapproved follow-on rather than widening this delivery.

In Scope

  • Removing complete-registry association validation from New Tag.
  • Relying on generated identity plus the atomic exclusive-create write, without registry or document-inventory uniqueness preflight.
  • Evidence-led discovery of the actual link-management UI need.
  • An ordered doc_url array of canonical cross-scope document locations.
  • A guarded v4-to-v5 migration and tag-description retirement.
  • Live document and report-title resolution without registry title duplication.
  • One reusable, provider-driven published-document location picker with a required consumer scope allowlist.
  • Provider coverage over public Analysis, Library, and published sub-scope projections, with Analysis-only title search in Tag Editor.
  • Edit Tag title-only listing plus draft exact-URL append and remove.
  • Tag Registry comma-separated document-title links.
  • Optional, multiple, shared, resolving, stale, and unlinked relationship states.

Not In Scope

  • Synchronizing tag group with document content or metadata.
  • Making tags own document deletion or documents own tag deletion.
  • Inferring, deduplicating, or automatically repairing associations.
  • Reordering document URLs.
  • Editing document titles or content from Tag Registry.
  • Bulk link mutation.
  • Automatically supporting every configured Docs scope or sub-scope.
  • An implicit all-supported-scopes picker mode.
  • Persisting fragments, temporary filters, or other incidental viewer state.
  • Searching source, manage-only, hidden, local-only, or unpublished documents.
  • Adding authoring controls to the live public site.
  • Integrating the picker into a second local authoring workflow in this delivery.
  • Redesigning the Analysis Concepts collection or generic sub-scope report.
  • Tag semantic-token implementation.
  • Renaming tag_id, adding a Concept identity model, or changing alias and assignment semantics.

Starting Authority

  • creation planner and transaction: studio/services/tags/tag_document_creation.py
  • focused row creation: studio/services/tags/tag_registry_mutations.py
  • API boundary: studio/app/server/studio/studio_tag_api/registry.py
  • current Tag Registry route and modules: studio/app/frontend/routes/tag-registry.html and studio/app/frontend/js/tag-registry-*
  • current local search-list interaction reference: shared/frontend/js/search-list.js
  • public scope configuration, search, sub-scope manifests, and canonical route projection: site/docs-viewer/config/defaults/docs-viewer-public-config.json, site/assets/data/search/, site/assets/data/docs/scopes/, site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-configured-scope-provider.js, and docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/sub_scope.py
  • canonical registry: studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-registry.json
  • Analysis document source: docs-viewer/scopes/analysis/source/sub-scopes/tags/documents/
  • focused creation, registry, workflow, and route tests: studio/tests/python/test_tag_document_creation.py, test_tag_registry_mutations.py, test_studio_tag_workflows.py, and the maintained Tag Registry smoke checks

These are inspection starting points. The picker remains local, app-neutral authoring behavior; Tag transport and mutation remain Studio-owned, while its search inputs, public placement data, and canonical URLs remain Docs Viewer-owned.

Completion Gate

Complete only when the New Tag prerequisite is independently accepted, the v5 migration and description retirement are reconciled, the shared provider and picker have a real Tag Registry consumer, the exact inspect/add/remove workflow is shipped and realistically reviewed, and durable owners describe the resulting current behavior without turning URL order or bootstrap output into ownership or one-to-one relationship invariants.
